requested_parts: Number of Escape Pods selected in a four-player game.
How the selected Pods are assigned to Sections and oriented at setup.
Which tokens start in the Intruder bag.
answers.answer: 1. Select 3 Escape Pods for four players. 2. Place the lowest-numbered Pod in Section A, the next in Section B, then alternate A/B; all start with the Locked side face up. 3. The Intruder bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player; for four players, that is 7 Adults total.
answers.evidence:
1–2 players: 2 pods, 3–4 players: 3 pods, 5 players: 4 pods. Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section "A", the next (in numerical order) in Section "B", then alternate A/B. All pods start with their Locked side face up.
Put these Intruder tokens in the Intruder bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player. Inference for four players: 3 base Adults + 4 additional Adults = 7 Adults.

requested_parts: How Objectives are filtered and dealt.
When each player chooses one Objective.
What happens to the rejected Objective card.
Whether Eggs trigger the choice.
answers.answer: 1. Let P be the actual player count; remove from both Corporate and Personal decks every card requiring more than P players, shuffle the decks separately, and deal each player one Corporate and one Personal Objective, kept hidden. 2. At the First Encounter—the first time an Intruder miniature appears on the board—each player immediately chooses one of their two Objectives. 3. Remove the unchosen Objective from the game face down, unseen by anyone; players may never look at other players’ removed Objectives. Then resolve the triggering Encounter. 4. Eggs do not trigger this choice.
answers.evidence:
Let P be the actual number of players in this game. Remove from both Objective decks (Corporate and Personal) every card requiring more than P players. Shuffle the two decks separately and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective card, kept hidden.
First Encounter: the first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others' removed Objectives). Then the triggering Encounter is resolved. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.

requested_parts: What is discarded to pay an Action card with printed cost 2, given the stated hand.
Whether Contamination cards can substitute for payment.
How an OR effect is handled.
answers.answer: 1. Discard the played Action card and the two other Action cards to pay the printed cost of 2; all three Action cards are used. The two Contamination cards remain in hand. 2. Contamination cards cannot substitute for any Action-cost payment. 3. If the Action card has sections separated by OR, choose one section/effect.
answers.evidence:
To use one, discard that card face up and pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards. If a card has two sections separated by "OR," choose one.
Action card: discard the card + its printed cost in extra cards.
Contamination cards are not Action cards: they can never be discarded to pay any Action cost.

requested_parts: When the Character takes Fire damage after taking one Action and passing in a burning Room.
Whether they can take further Actions during this Player Phase.
Whether they may discard cards when passing.
Whether later players’ rounds cause further Fire wounds to them that turn.
answers.answer: 1. They take 1 Light Wound at the end of their own passing round, after declaring Pass. 2. They cannot take further normal Actions during the rest of the Player Phase, though Interruption remains permitted if its requirements are met. 3. At the moment they pass, they may discard any number of cards from their hand. 4. Later players’ rounds do not cause them further Fire wounds that turn.
answers.evidence:
If you perform only 1 Action instead of two, you must pass.
When passing, flip your Help card to its "Pass" side and apply the passing rules below.
A Character who ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound (every round; only after finishing their own round — passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn).
At the moment you pass, you may discard any number of cards from your hand.
After you pass: You cannot take further normal Actions; Interruption remains permitted as below.
Fire in your Room: Take 1 Light Wound at the end of your own passing round. Later players' rounds do not give you further Fire wounds that turn.
Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.

requested_parts: What happens to the tile on entering an unexplored Room.
How the Item Counter is set.
How the Exploration effect resolves and where its token goes.
When a Noise roll is made on entry to the described empty Room.
How Silence, Danger, and an occupied destination affect the Noise roll.
answers.answer: 1. Flip the unexplored Room tile face up, reveal and resolve its Exploration token. 2. For an ordinary Room tile, rotate it until the token’s Item number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board; the Nest and Room Covered With Slime are exceptions with no Item count. 3. Resolve the token’s effect (including Silence or Danger if shown), then remove the Exploration token from the game into the box. 4. Because the destination is empty, after resolving exploration make the ordinary Noise roll unless the Exploration result was Silence or Danger, which replaces that roll. 5. Silence causes no Noise roll; Danger resolves its Intruder movement/noise procedure instead of a roll. If another Character or Intruder is already in the destination Room, do not roll Movement Noise.
answers.evidence:
After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule. A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward. Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders). If anyone — Character or Intruder — is already there, do NOT roll for Movement Noise.
Item Counter: the Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count. For other Room tiles, rotate the tile until the Exploration token's number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board next to the slot.
Silence — no Movement Noise roll. Nothing happens. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead.
Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.
After resolving an Exploration token, remove it from the game into the box; it does not return to a supply or stay on the Room (each is resolved only once, on first entry).

requested_parts: Careful Movement’s cost and what it replaces.
When Careful Movement is forbidden.
Whether a Closed Door may be crossed.
Whether a miniature may stop in a Corridor.
answers.answer: 1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards; instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination Room. It also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with that chosen Noise placement. 2. It cannot be used in Combat or when all Corridors connected to the destination already have Noise markers. 3. No: a Closed Door blocks player Movement between the connected Rooms. 4. No one may stop in a Corridor; Characters and Intruders occupy Rooms only (Escape Pods are the exception for Characters).
answers.evidence:
Careful Movement (cost 2) — follows normal Movement restrictions, including Closed Doors blocking passage; but instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter. You cannot Carefully Move if all Corridors connected to the destination already hold Noise markers, and you cannot use it while in Combat. The FAQ clarifies that Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too.
Characters and Intruders may only occupy Rooms (Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines — count as Rooms; Escape Pod tokens are the only exception for Characters). Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor.
A Closed Door blocks the "neighboring" status for players' Movement.

requested_parts: The Encounter sequence when a Noise result directs placement into a Corridor that already has Noise, including a Technical Corridors Entrance.
Which Noise markers are removed.
Where the drawn token goes.
How Surprise Attack is determined.
Whether Contamination cards count in the comparison.
answers.answer: 1. Placing a Noise marker where one already exists resolves an Encounter. Discard all Noise markers in Corridors connected to the Room, including the Technical Corridors space if the Room has an Entrance; then draw one Intruder token. 2. Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned (it may return if an Intruder of that type later hides by entering Technical Corridors). 3. Place its matching Intruder miniature in the Room. Compare the drawn token’s number with the number of cards in the triggering player’s hand, counting Action and Contamination cards: fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack against that Character; equal or more causes no Surprise Attack. 4. Yes, Contamination cards count as hand cards for this comparison.
answers.evidence:
A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.
An Encounter is any instance of an Intruder appearing (via an Intruder-bag draw) in a Room where a Character is present. Resolve: Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance). Draw 1 Intruder token from the bag (symbol on one side, number on the other). Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned. A Blank follows its separate return procedure below. Place the matching Intruder miniature in the Room. Compare the token's number to the number of cards in the triggering player's hand (Action AND Contamination cards both count). Fewer cards than the number → Surprise Attack (an Intruder Attack against that Character). Equal or more → nothing happens.
The token kept aside may return to the bag if an Intruder of that type later hides by entering the Technical Corridors.

requested_parts: How Danger resolves when several eligible neighboring Intruders exist.
What happens when no Intruders are eligible.
Whether an Intruder moving into a Character’s Room is an Encounter.
How Slime affects Silence.
answers.answer: 1. All eligible Intruders in neighboring Rooms move into the Room; eligible means not in Combat with any Character. 2. If none are eligible, place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one, counting the Technical Corridors space if the Room has an Entrance. 3. No. An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is not an Encounter; the Character and Intruder are simply in Combat. 4. With a Slime marker, a Silence result becomes Danger.
answers.evidence:
Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.
An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter (they are simply in Combat).
Slime marker: while on your board, every "Silence" result (Noise roll or Exploration token) becomes "Danger."

requested_parts: What happens to Noise and the Blank token during a Blank Encounter.
When an Adult is added during a Blank Encounter.
How Blank resolves during Intruder bag development.
answers.answer: 1. In a Blank Encounter, place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to the Room; return the Blank to the bag, and the Encounter ends with no miniature appearing. 2. Add 1 Adult token to the bag only if the Blank was the last token in the bag, and only if an Adult token is available. 3. During bag development, Blank adds 1 Adult token to the bag if any are available, otherwise nothing happens, then the Blank is returned to the bag; this branch does not specify the last-token condition.
answers.evidence:
Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears).
Blank — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens). Return the Blank token to the bag.

requested_parts: Where two Intruders attempting to move through the same Closed Door from the same Room end up.
What happens to the Door.
Whether a Destroyed Door can later be closed.
Whether a Closed Door blocks an Intruder appearing due to a Noise roll.
answers.answer: 1. Both stay in the Room they attempted to leave. 2. They destroy the Closed Door simultaneously; it becomes a lying, Destroyed token. 3. Only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door. 4. No: if a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.
answers.evidence:
Closed = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws). An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put). Destroyed = lying token: movement allowed; only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it.
If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.

requested_parts: What happens to the Intruder miniature when an injured Intruder moves into Technical Corridors.
What happens to its Injury markers.
What happens to its token.
What happens to Noise already in the Technical Corridors space.
Whether Characters or Doors normally use those Corridors.
answers.answer: 1. The Intruder disappears into the ducts and its miniature is removed from the board. 2. Discard all its Injury markers. 3. Return its token to the Intruder bag. 4. The Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is not removed. 5. Characters cannot use Technical Corridors except with the Mechanic’s Technical Corridors Action card or the Technical Corridor Plans Item; Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence:
If an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts: discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature from the board. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is NOT removed by this.
Some Rooms have Technical Corridors Entrances, all linked to the single Technical Corridors space. Characters can never use them (the only exceptions: the Mechanic's "Technical Corridors" Action card and the "Technical Corridor Plans" Item card).
Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.

requested_parts: Shoot and Melee Action-card costs and Ammo cost.
Where the target Intruder must be.
Melee Contamination procedure.
What happens on an ordinary miss for Shoot and Melee.
What the double-hit die face does in each attack.
answers.answer: 1. Each is a Basic Action costing 1 Action card. Shoot also requires a Weapon in Hand with at least 1 Ammo and discards 1 Ammo. 2. Choose one target Intruder in your Room. 3. Melee draws 1 Contamination card and puts it on top of your Action discard pile before choosing a target and rolling; it cannot pay the Action cost. 4. A Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries and no Wound to the shooter; a Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and gives the attacker 1 Serious Wound. 5. A double-hit result deals 2 Injuries in Shoot before Weapon modifiers, but only 1 Injury in Melee.
answers.evidence:
Shoot (cost 1): requires a Weapon in Hand with at least 1 Ammo. (1) Choose a Weapon and 1 target Intruder in your Room; (2) discard 1 Ammo from the Weapon card; (3) roll the Combat die.
Melee Attack (cost 1): (1) draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile; (2) choose 1 target Intruder in your Room; (3) roll the Combat die. Results mirror Shooting with two changes: any miss also inflicts 1 Serious Wound on your Character, and the 2-Injury result deals only 1 Injury (in melee, rolls of 2 Hits are treated as 1 Hit).
Ordinary attack misses: a Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries to the target and causes no Wound to the shooter. A Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and causes 1 Serious Wound to the attacker.
Double-hit symbol: 2 Injuries to any Intruder type before Weapon modifiers (Shoot); 1 Injury to any Intruder type (Melee).

requested_parts: How a Larva’s death is checked.
How an Adult’s death is checked and when its Carcass is placed.
How a Queen’s death is checked and when its Carcass is placed.
What a Queen Retreat arrow does during the check.
answers.answer: 1. A Larva dies at 1 Injury; its miniature is removed and no Carcass is placed. 2. For an Adult, draw 1 Intruder Attack card and use its blood value: if blood is less than or equal to its current total Injuries, it dies; if it dies, remove the miniature and place a Carcass in the Room. 3. For a Queen, draw 2 Attack cards and sum their blood values; if the sum is less than or equal to its current total Injuries, it dies, and on death its Carcass is placed in the Room. 4. If either of the Queen’s two cards shows a Retreat arrow, she retreats instead of resolving a numerical endurance/death result: draw an Event card and move her through the Corridor number in its Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card.
answers.evidence:
Intruder Injuries and death: after any Injuries, put that many Injury markers on the Intruder's base and check its Injury Effect. Compare current total Injuries, not just the latest hit.
Larva: 1 Injury kills | Remove miniature; no Carcass.
Adult: Draw 1 Intruder Attack card; use only its blood value. Blood ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. | Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room.
Queen: Draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood values. Sum ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. | Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room.
During an Injury Effect check, if any drawn card's blood icon contains the Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of a numerical endurance/death result. The Intruder flees: draw an Event card and move the Intruder through the Corridor whose number appears in that card's Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card. The Queen and Breeders retreat if EITHER of their 2 drawn cards shows the Retreat symbol.

requested_parts: When the two Intruder attacks occur during Escape and their order.
Who is targeted by Escape attacks.
What happens to the Character’s Corpse if they die.
What happens if they survive, including entering the unexplored empty Room.
answers.answer: 1. Before moving, resolve one separate Intruder Attack for each Intruder present, starting with the larger one (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva). 2. The Escape attack targets the escaper. 3. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to Escape from. 4. If they survive, complete the move to the neighboring Room; because it is unexplored, reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then apply Movement Noise as usual. Since it is empty, roll Noise unless the Exploration result was Silence or Danger, which replaces the roll.
answers.evidence:
To leave a Room containing Intruders, perform a Movement Action (cost 1) to a neighboring Room (explored or unexplored). BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva; FAQ Rules 5). If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if the destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored). If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room you tried to Escape from.
An Escape attack targets the escaper.
After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule. A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward. Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders).

requested_parts: How the target is chosen when several Characters share the Room and how a tie is broken.
How an ordinary Intruder Attack hit is determined.
What is different for a Larva attack.
Where the Larva’s Contamination card goes.
answers.answer: 1. The Intruder targets the Character whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; on a tie, the Character with the First Player token is targeted (or the next player in turn order). 2. For a non-Larva, draw 1 Intruder Attack card; a symbol matching the attacking Intruder’s type means resolve the card’s effect, otherwise the attack misses. Ignore the blood icon. 3. A Larva draws no Attack card: remove its miniature from the board, put it on the target’s Character board, and give the target 1 Contamination card. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears and the target only gains the Contamination card; this does not automatically kill them. 4. The Contamination card is drawn from its deck and placed on top of the target’s Action discard pile.
answers.evidence:
Choose the target: the Intruder attacks a Character in its Room — with several Characters present, the one whose player has the FEWEST Action cards in hand; on a tie, the Character with the First Player token (or the next player in turn order).
For other Intruders, draw 1 Intruder Attack card: if it shows a symbol matching the attacking Intruder's type, resolve the card's effect; otherwise the attack misses. Ignore the blood icon during attacks.
A Larva does not draw Attack cards. Instead: remove the Larva miniature from the board and place it on the target's Character board (on the miniature picture), and the target gains 1 Contamination card. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing one stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them (FAQ Rules 12).
When a Character "gets a Contamination card," draw it from the Contamination deck and place it on top of their Action discard pile.

requested_parts: Whether dressing one Serious Wound prevents death from a further Light Wound when the Character has three Serious Wounds.
What happens on a third Light Wound otherwise.
What Heal can remove.
Where the Corpse and Heavy Objects go when the Character dies.
answers.answer: 1. No. Dressing only ignores the card’s effect; it still counts toward the three-wound limit, and dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when already at three Serious Wounds. 2. On a third Light Wound, clear the Light Wound track and suffer a Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies. 4. On death, place the Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence:
Light Wounds: track on your Character board — 1st marker on the upper space, 2nd on the lower space (= 2 Light Wounds); on a 3rd, clear the track and suffer a Serious Wound.
A Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies instantly upon suffering ANY additional Wound (Light or Serious). Remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room (now a Character Corpse Object), and drop all their Heavy Objects there.
Dress a Serious Wound: flip the card face down — its effect is ignored, but it still counts toward the 3-wound limit. Dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when you already have 3 Serious Wounds. Heal: remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies.

requested_parts: Which Contamination cards Canteen/Shower scan and remove.
How an Infected result affects the Character with or without a Larva.
Which cards Surgery scans and removes and what it does with a Larva.
Surgery’s payment and turn consequences.
answers.answer: 1. Canteen and Shower may scan all Contamination cards in the Character’s hand; remove every non-Infected scanned card from the game. 2. Infected cards are kept. If no Larva was already on the Character board, place a Larva; if one was already there, the Character dies and a Creeper is placed in the death Room. 3. Surgery scans all Contamination cards in the Action deck, hand, and discard pile, removes all Infected cards from the game, and removes a Larva from the board if present. 4. Surgery is a Room Action costing 2 Action cards and requires being in that Room, out of Combat, and no Malfunction there. Then suffer 1 Light Wound, automatically pass, and shuffle all cards, including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards, into the Action deck; the hand stays empty until next turn.
answers.evidence:
Canteen — Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (an Infected result places a Larva on your board — with a Larva already there, you die and a Creeper appears in your Room).
For the optional Canteen/Shower hand scan: Non-Infected — Remove the scanned non-Infected card from the game. Infected, no Larva already on board — Keep the Infected card; place a Larva on Character board. Infected, Larva already on board — Keep the Infected card; Character dies; place 1 Creeper in the death Room.
Surgery — Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all your cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until the next turn.
Room Action: discard 2 Action cards while in that Room, out of Combat and without a Malfunction there (unless an explicit special ability overrides location).

requested_parts: How Shoot and Melee destroy uncarried Eggs.
How Grenade destroys them.
How Molotov and Fire destroy them.
Which Melee penalties are waived on a missed Egg attack.
When Noise is rolled and where for remote Grenade/Molotov attacks.
When the Nest is destroyed.
answers.answer: 1. Each Injury from Shoot or Melee destroys 1 uncarried Egg. 2. Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; uncarried Eggs let the Room be targeted as if an Intruder were there. 3. Molotov destroys 1 Egg immediately; its Fire marker can destroy further Eggs during later Event Phase Fire Damage steps. A Fire marker normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg per such step; Vulnerability to Fire raises destruction from the Nest Egg pool to 2 per step. 4. A missed Egg Melee causes neither the normal Contamination gain nor the Serious Wound for a miss; the summary leaves unresolved how the normal pre-roll draw timing interacts with this miss exception. 5. Roll Noise after every Shoot, Melee, Grenade, or Molotov attempt, including a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll in your own Room, not the Nest. 6. When no Eggs remain—whether carried away or destroyed—the Nest is destroyed and marked with 1 Injury marker.
answers.evidence:
Egg tokens on the Intruder board represent the Eggs in the Nest; taking or destroying Eggs removes them from the Intruder board. When no Eggs remain (all carried away or destroyed), the Nest is destroyed — mark it with 1 Injury marker.
Shoot or Melee: Each Injury destroys 1 Egg. Resolve the normal attack, with the Egg Melee exception below.
Grenade: Destroys 2 Eggs. Uncarried Eggs permit the Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there.
Molotov Cocktail: Destroys 1 Egg immediately; its Fire marker can continue destroying Eggs in later Fire Damage steps.
Fire marker: Normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase Fire Damage step. For the Nest's Egg pool, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to 2 per step (FAQ Rooms 7).
A successful Egg Melee retains the normal draw of 1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. The manuals do not specify how to reconcile the normal pre-roll Contamination step with this miss exception; no refund or alternative draw timing is specified.
After every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, perform a Noise roll, including a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll in your own Room, not the Nest (FAQ Rooms 2).

requested_parts: What permits entry to an Escape Pod and what prevents it.
What must be resolved before boarding and the failure condition.
How many Characters and Heavy Objects fit.
Options and consequences when waiting in a Pod.
answers.answer: 1. Use the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action (cost 2 Action cards). The Pod in that Section must be Unlocked and have a free Character space; entry is prohibited if the Section has an Intruder or Malfunction. 2. Roll Noise first; if an Intruder appears or reaches the Section, the attempt fails. 3. A Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character space. 4. After boarding, you may launch immediately: remove the Pod token and occupants’ miniatures from the game; they stop participating, count as arriving on Earth, and still face final Contamination and Objective checks. Choosing to wait makes you pass the current turn while remaining present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls. If an Intruder appears in the Section, every Character in any Pod there returns immediately to the Section Room. If another Character boards your Pod, that new boarder may immediately launch both occupants. If a Malfunction appears, waiting/launching/exiting remain available; only new entry is blocked. At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase, choose one: wait and pass, launch, or exit free into the Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions.
answers.evidence:
Board: pay 2 Action cards for the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action. A Pod there must be Unlocked with a free Character space. No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes entry fail.
Capacity: 2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space.
Launch immediately: after boarding you may launch. Remove the Pod token and its occupants' miniatures from the game; they stop participating and count as arriving on Earth. They still face the final Contamination and Objective checks.
Choosing to wait makes you pass the current turn, while you remain treated as present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls. While waiting, apply all three contingencies: if an Intruder appears in the Section, every Character in any of its Pods immediately returns to the Section Room; if another Character boards your Pod, that new boarder may immediately launch both occupants; if a Malfunction appears, your normal wait/launch/exit choices remain available and only new entry is blocked. At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase, choose wait and pass, launch, or exit free into the Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions.

requested_parts: Victory Check order.
The result of two Damaged Engines.
What a non-Earth destination does, including the Quarantine/Mars exception.
Contamination procedure for an infected survivor or one carrying a Larva.
Whether Escape Pod passengers undergo Contamination checks.
answers.answer: 1. Resolve Engines, then Coordinates, then Contamination, then Objectives. 2. answers.evidence:
Resolve Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives in that order.
Engines, only if the ship has survived: reveal all three top Engine tokens. 2 or 3 Damaged Engines make the ship explode. EVERYTHING aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders. Launched Pod passengers are already away.
Coordinates, only if the ship has survived: reveal the Coordinates card and read the destination selected by the Destination marker. Non-Earth kills hibernating Characters, while the ship is not destroyed and Intruders remain alive. A sleeper with the Quarantine Objective survives if the destination is Mars.
Contamination, for every surviving Character, including launched Pod passengers: At least one Infected card, OR a Larva already on board: shuffle all Action and Contamination cards from deck, hand and discard into a single new Action deck and draw the top 4 cards. Any Contamination card among those four kills you, whether Infected or not; four Action cards with no Contamination means you survive this check. A Larva skips the initial Scan but still requires this complete shuffle, draw and result check.
If no Larva is already on board, scan every Contamination card from Action deck, hand and discard pile. If none is Infected, there is no four-card draw.
